speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your chronic diarrhea and abdominal discomfort, I need to gather some specific details. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Have you experienced any unintended weight loss or fever during this period, and do your symptoms improve after you have a bowel movement?

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptom relief after bowel movements and the presence of mucus strongly suggest Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Diarrhea (IBS-D) or Inflammatory Bowel Disease. To distinguish between functional and organic causes, I need to assess for systemic signs of inflammation. Have you had any recent travel outside the country, and have you noticed any joint pain or skin rashes associated with your gastrointestinal symptoms?

text: The negative stool ova and parasites test rules out Giardia, so I need to look for other causes of chronic inflammation. REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Calprotectin

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal fecal calprotectin effectively rules out inflammatory bowel disease, pointing strongly toward a functional disorder like IBS-D. Have you noticed any specific foods that trigger your symptoms, or have you experienced significant stress or anxiety lately?
